title: ECHO-Check: Comparison of echocardiography using handheld ultrasound with standard devices in mature newborns
summary: The Department of Paediatric Cardiology at the LMU, with the support of the Department of Neonatology, is planning a clinical study to investigate the image quality of GE's wireless ultrasound devices (Vscan Air SL). The study will be conducted on 100 healthy newborns. The study population will be recruited from the maternity ward at the Großhadern Clinic and the portal clinic of the Ludwig Maximilian University. The results will be used to make a scientifically proven recommendation for the use of handheld ultrasound devices (HUD), which are already in use in some cases, but without a systematic comparison to the standard devices used to date. In the long term, proof of comparably good image quality should enable more outpatient use of portable ultrasound devices. This will make ultrasound examinations of the heart more financially attractive for practices, as there is no need to purchase expensive ultrasound equipment. In addition, the standard of care can be improved in financially weaker regions/countries where the funds for a stationary ultrasound machine are lacking.
conditions: Comparison of echocardiography with handheld ultrasound devices and standard devices

interventions.name: Newborns without prenatally or perinatally diagnosed heart disease receive a cardiac ultrasound with a handheld device and a standard device at one point in time. criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Newborns without prenatally or perinatally diagnosed heart disease may participate after informed consent has been obtained from their parents. The children are recruited from the neonatology ward at Großhadern Hospital and the Dr von Hauner Children's Hospital. The minimum age is set at 48 hours in order to wait for spontaneous closure of the ductus arteriosus botalli.
Exclusion criteria:
Children with prenatally known heart defects are excluded from the study. In addition, children for whom a comprehensive ultrasound examination is not fully possible (for technical reasons or because the child becomes restless) are subsequently excluded.
